plan.planning_summary: This portfolio tests three genuinely distinct strategy axes for a dual-band mid-IR bandpass filter on CaF2 substrate. Route 1 explores the classic high-contrast ZnS/MgF2 material pair with dual-cavity topology - the established IR coating approach. Route 2 tests an alternative Si/SiO2 material pair with identical topology to isolate material absorption effects in the 4+ μm region. Route 3 tests whether topology matters more than materials by using a single-cavity defect-engineered structure with ZnS/MgF2. These axes can disagree: if Routes 1 and 2 both fail but Route 3 succeeds, topology is the limiting factor; if Route 1 succeeds but Route 2 fails, material absorption at 4+ μm is critical. Literature L01, L17, L21, and L28 inform material selection and Bragg pair methodology, but none guarantee this specific dual-band requirement will be met within 24 layers.

routes.title: ZnS/MgF2 Dual-Cavity Dual-Band Bandpass Filter
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A dual-cavity Fabry-Perot structure using ZnS/MgF2 Bragg pairs can simultaneously achieve high transmission at 3.25-3.35 μm and 4.20-4.30 μm while suppressing 2.50-3.10 μm and 4.45-5.00 μm within 22 layers.
routes.design_principle: High refractive index contrast between ZnS (n~2.4) and MgF2 (n~1.35) in mid-IR enables strong Bragg reflection with fewer layer pairs. Two optical cavities separated by a central Bragg mirror create two transmission peaks at designed wavelengths. Literature L01 and L17 demonstrate ZnS-based multilayers on CaF2 for MWIR applications.

routes.title: Si/SiO2 Dual-Cavity Dual-Band Bandpass Filter
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A dual-cavity Fabry-Perot structure using Si/SiO2 Bragg pairs can achieve comparable dual-band transmission to ZnS/MgF2 while potentially reducing absorption in the 4.45-5.00 μm suppression band.
routes.design_principle: Si (n~3.4) and SiO2 (n~1.4) provide even higher index contrast than ZnS/MgF2, potentially enabling fewer layers or sharper band edges. routes.title: ZnS/MgF2 Single-Cavity Defect-Engineered Dual-Band Filter
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A single-cavity structure with carefully engineered defect layers in the Bragg mirror can produce two transmission peaks without requiring two separate cavities, reducing total layer count while maintaining dual-band performance.
routes.design_principle: Introducing controlled defects (thickness variations) within a Bragg mirror creates localized states that produce transmission peaks within the stopband. Two defects at different positions can create two peaks. This topology uses fewer layers than dual-cavity but requires more precise thickness control. L28 discusses Bragg pair constraints for complex filter design.

harness. This is not route planning and you must not redesign the route.

{"selections":[{"request_id":"material_01","selected_rank":1,"provider":"rii_sqlite","dataset_id":562,"reason":"..."}]}

Choose exactly one candidate from the supplied list for every request. Never
invent, rename, or edit a provider or dataset_id. The selected_rank must point
to the selected array element, and provider/dataset_id must copy that element.

explicit requested source are hard constraints. A candidate with
formula_exact=false or semantic_match=same_element_family is not an allowed
substitute for a formula request. SiO is not SiO2, even if the SiO2 candidate
has better physical coverage. When several candidates satisfy the hard
constraints, select the highest-ranked one (usually rank 1). If no candidate
satisfies them, return selected_rank:null, provider:null, dataset_id:null and
reason:"needs_confirmation" for that request.

plan.planning_summary: This control axis tests a dual-cavity bandpass filter topology optimized from recalled thin-film design principles. The hypothesis is that two Fabry-Perot cavities separated by distributed Bragg reflectors can simultaneously transmit the methane (3.25-3.35 μm) and CO2 (4.20-4.30 μm) bands while blocking the suppression bands. The design uses ZnS/MgF2 as the high/low index pair based on recalled IR transparency and index contrast. This route optimizes individual layer thicknesses while keeping the 22-layer topology fixed. What I would have wanted to look up: exact refractive indices of ZnS and MgF2 at 3-5 μm, CaF2 substrate index dispersion, and published dual-band filter designs for validation.

Optimize all 22 layer thicknesses individually to maximize transmittance in 3250-3350 nm and 4200-4300 nm bands while minimizing transmittance in 2500-3100 nm and 4450-5000 nm bands. No metal layers. Total layer count is exactly 22. Materials are zns and mgf2 from the material catalog. Substrate is Daimon-20. Incidence is from air side at normal incidence (0 degrees). Wavelength range of interest is 2500-5000 nm.

expected_observations: If the dual-cavity hypothesis holds, best_target_score should increase across optimization rounds as thicknesses converge toward values that create transmission peaks at both target bands
valid_candidates should remain high (above 50% of generated candidates) if the thickness search space is well-bounded
tightest_margin should not systematically decrease across rounds, indicating the design remains physically realizable
If the hypothesis fails, best_target_score will plateau early and transmission peaks will not align with both target bands simultaneously
stop_conditions: if best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
if valid_candidates falls below 20% of generated candidates for two consecutive rounds, relax thickness bounds and continue for one more round before stopping
if tightest_margin becomes negative for three consecutive rounds, reduce maximum thickness limits and continue
